prompt:
You describe a block diagram or schematic from an electronics datasheet for an engineer who cannot see it.

Cover, in this order:
1. What the diagram shows overall, in one sentence.
2. Every block or component, by its label.
3. Every connection: which block connects to which, the signal or pin names on it, and the direction of any arrows.
4. Every voltage, frequency, part value or other number shown, with its unit.

Figure type: block diagram or schematic
Section: 6 Mounting recommendations > 6.3 Mechanical stress maximum on the PCB
Caption: Figure 4: Mechanical stress maximum on the PCB
Text inside the figure (read from this image by a specialised OCR model; use these spellings): PCB | sensor | anchor point (e.g., screw) | Keep distance !
Text that mentions the figure: Figure 4 shows a stress maximum in the center of the diagonal crossover of the four anchor points. It is good manufacturing practice to always avoid or reduce mechanical stress by optimizing the PCB design first, then placing the sensor in an appropriate low-stress area.

Rules:
- When a name or number from "Text inside the figure" is visible in the image, copy it exactly, character for character.
- Never invent a value, name, pin, unit or connection. If something is too small or blurry to read, write "unreadable" instead of guessing.
- Describe only what this image shows. Do not explain general theory or add advice.
- Mention each item once. Stop when everything is covered.
- Plain text only: no Markdown headings, tables or bold. Short paragraphs and "- " lists are fine.
- Start directly with what the figure is (for example "Block diagram of ..."), not with "The image shows".

answer.text:
Block diagram of mechanical stress maximum on the PCB.

Components:
PCB
sensor
anchor point (e.g., screw)

Connections:
The PCB contains four anchor points (e.g., screw) located at the corners.
The PCB contains a sensor located near the center where the diagonal lines cross.
The diagram shows two states: one where the sensor is placed in a high-stress area (left image) and one where the sensor is placed in a low-stress area (right image).
In the right image, there are dashed boxes around the sensor area with checkmarks, and an arrow points from the sensor area to the text "Keep distance !".

Values:
No voltage, frequency, part value, or other number with a unit is shown.
